key_insight: AI agents can exploit structure in computational algebra to solve more systems within a fixed budget, but reasoning costs can offset computational savings.
engineering_relevance: Persistent memory and reusable solver compilation offer ways to accelerate repeated algebraic workloads, with trade-offs in strategy quality and upfront cost.
method: Use benchmark families of algebraic systems with controlled shared structure.
Evaluate agents on independent instances and related-instance streams with persistent memory.
Have agents compile fast, reusable solvers for known problem families.
evidence_signal: Experiments across three settings show expanded solvability within fixed budgets, reduced repeated-solving costs with memory, and faster reusable solvers after compilation.
watch_item: Net efficiency gains depend on amortizing reasoning and compilation overhead, while memory may retain suboptimal strategies.
